name: Sodium hypophosphite
description: Sodium hypophosphite (CAS 7681-53-0 ), commercially abbreviated as SHP and also known as sodium phosphinate, is an inorganic phosphorus salt used industrially as a reducing agent and catalyst. It is essential in electroless metal plating and polymer stabilization. Its reducing capacity drives controlled chemical reactions across multiple manufacturing sectors, ensuring high-performance results in industrial settings. In electroless nickel plating, SHP acts as the primary reducing agent, enabling uniform metal deposition on complex or non-conductive substrates without an external electrical current. This is a critical process in electronics. Automotive and aerospace component manufacturing also rely on this technology. Polymer producers use SHP as a catalyst and stabilizer in the production of polyamides, where it controls molecular weight and prevents discoloration. In water treatment, it functions as a sequestrant to inhibit scale formation and metal ion interference in industrial cooling and boiler systems. This helps maintain the efficiency and longevity of heavy machinery. Pharmaceutical and food-grade applications include its use as an antioxidant and preservative in formulations where phosphorus-based reduction chemistry is required. It ensures stability and safety in sensitive products. Sodium hypophosphite is supplied as a white crystalline powder or as an aqueous solution, typically at 50% concentration. Recognized grades include technical, food-grade meeting FCC specifications, and pharmaceutical-grade. These pharmaceutical grades often meet USP or BP standards.
